Len's success was largely due to a fine burst of speed at the finish. Another fine effort was by Fred Clay, who pulled up yards on his opponents in the relay.

The chief feature of the race was the forward running of several of the younger school, particularly Stan Eeles who perhaps ran his best race to date—Stan has the makings of a real runner if he will get down to it, Fred Clay, John Brown, Bob Boyden, Norman Walker and Alf Heathfield.
Fred Clay was married this summer and has moved to Leicester. Congratulations and best wishes to you both for your future health and prosperity.

Fred Clay, feeling the effects of a strenuous afternoon the previous Saturday at Dartford, lost his heat in the 100, but won his 220 yards first heat in 24.4, but failed to qualify in the second round.

As it was a close match resulted, and grand performances were put up by our sprinters, Jack Frost and Fred Clay, against such opposition, with Jack Brown, our A.A.A. junior 880 yards champion, others giving their usual sterling performances.
Fred Clay has lent valuable assistance, as have Bert Machell and Alan Fleming. This is another event in which we shall have to unearth some new talent.

Owing to the forward running of Dick Tobin 5, and Tom Clinton 7, our "B" team gained second awards, and our congratulations go to Charlie Smart and John Weames, who completed the "B" team. Tom Morrell and Fred Clay also ran well, as did Bert Mitchell, N.
